newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Airlines mulls leasing Boeing-737.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Airlines mulls leasing Boeing-737.

text.p: Lithunia's transport ministry said on Thursday that Lithuanian Airlines planned to lease one more Boeing 737-300 aircraft in the autumn and was considering transatlantic flights next year.
"We want to lease one more Boeing aircraft in autumn," Algis Zhvaliauskas, the minister of transport, told a news conference but declined to provide more details on the deal.
He said that the aircraft would be used on the flights to Dubai via Georgia and other "routes to the South".
"If everything goes smoothly, next year we are planning to acquire a Boeing 767 and to start transatlantic flights," Zhvaliauskas said.
"It is our programme maximum," he added.

State-run Lithuanian Airlines, which is to be merged with the smaller Air Lietuva later this year, currently has a fleet of three Boeing 737-200s, two Saab 340 Bs, a Jet Star 731 and 11 Russian-built Jak-42s.
Lithuania's government says it wants to sell off the company but that at least 51 percent will have to remain in Lithuanian hands to preserve its status as national carrier.
